themes.topic: Hierarchical authority of smṛti sources in resolving śrāddha disputes

mentions.quote: in these verses of Śaṅkha, the Brahma Purāṇa, Manu, etc., only Trayodaśī conjoined with Maghā is heard as the time for the śrāddha, yet even the plain tithi is a time for śrāddha
the verses of Manu and Viṣṇu, which state a plain Trayodaśī…are explanatory statements (arthavāda), and since it is possible for them to have syntactical unity with a direct injunction

themes.justification: Throughout this window the Vīramitrodaya systematically ranks competing smṛti passages as direct injunctions (vidhi) versus explanatory statements (arthavāda) to resolve apparent contradictions about śrāddha timing.

themes.topic: Obligatory (nitya) versus optional (kāmya) classification of śrāddha occasions

mentions.quote: And this is obligatory (nitya).
And it is also optional (kāmya).
And from the word 'even' (api) in 'even water on these,' they are obligatory.
Śūlapāṇi, however, says that since this is without foundation, they are only optional.

themes.justification: A major organising dichotomy of the section is whether each śrāddha time generates a binding duty or merely an elective opportunity for additional merit.

themes.topic: Cosmological time-units (Yugas, Manvantaras, Kalpas) as śrāddha occasion

mentions.quote: these four tithis are said by the ancients to be Yugādyās, of infinite merit. / A restrained man should give to the ancestors even water mixed with sesame on these.
these are the Manvantarādis, making what is given imperishable
these thirty are the Kalpas, the tithis of the Supreme Lord. / Their commencement tithis have been stated by me as most meritorious.

themes.justification: A large section of this window catalogues Yugādis, Yugāntas, Manvantarādis, and Kalpādis as special śrāddha occasions whose cosmic scale magnifies the merit of any gift given on those days.

themes.topic: Astrological and calendrical determination of auspicious śrāddha time

mentions.quote: The Uttaras, Śravaṇa, Tiṣya, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Prajāpati, / Hasta, Śatabhiṣaj, Svāti, Citrā, the ancestral one, and Aśvinī, // these nakṣatras are always praised in a rite for the ancestors.
Vyatīpāta is the seventeenth yoga among the Viṣkumbha, etc., yogas. A special rule for its ghaṭikās is in the science of astronomy
The Kalpataru says that Vyatīpāta is the equality of the declination of the sun and moon, which is to be known from the science of astronomy.

themes.justification: The window extensively deploys nakṣatra, tithi, yoga, and solar-ingress astronomy to determine when śrāddha is most efficacious, grounding ritual law in astronomical observation.

themes.topic: Restrictions on śrāddha for those with living sons versus those without

mentions.quote: Or, it applies to a householder with a son. / A householder with a son should not perform a śrāddha on Trayodaśī.
He who is without offspring, for him Trayodaśī is proclaimed for a śrāddha. / He who has offspring and performs it, his lineage is destroyed.

themes.justification: The Caturdaśī and Trayodaśī discussions both turn on whether the performer has living male descendants, generating a differential rule structure based on progeny status.

themes.topic: Death anniversary (kṣayāha) and violent/untimely death as special śrāddha occasions

mentions.quote: For those killed by poison, a snake, a beast of prey, fire, a wild animal, or a Brahmin, / the rites should be performed on Caturdaśī
For those who have an untimely death, or a death by a weapon, / and for those who have died in an epidemic…a śrāddha should be performed for them on Caturdaśī
Year after year, it should be performed for one's mother and father on the day of death.

themes.justification: The Caturdaśī section and the closing kṣayāha section both focus on how the manner and date of death create special śrāddha obligations separate from regular calendar-based śrāddhas.

themes.topic: Conflict resolution between contradictory scriptural passages via hermeneutical principles

mentions.quote: Being determined as different by their form, and not desiring each other, / they seek their purpose with disregard for each other.
If, for the sake of the simplicity of inferring a single injunction, one were to resort to the indication of another, which is not desired, even by superseding the natural independence

themes.justification: The text applies a recognised exegetical principle (maxim of independent injunctions) to navigate between competing smṛti positions, reflecting the broader Mīmāṃsā hermeneutics underlying dharmaśāstra digests.

themes.topic: Ritual pollution (āśauca) as disqualifier interrupting ongoing śrāddha sequences

mentions.quote: in the fortnight-śrāddha, even if an agreement is made with the Brahmins only once…if the Brahmins incur impurity (āśauca), they must be dismissed.
if impurity befalls him in the middle…the rule 'there is no impurity in a rite that has been commenced' does not apply, and the commenced abhyāsa option must be abandoned.

themes.justification: The opening paragraphs of the window treat āśauca as the primary contingency that suspends or invalidates an ongoing śrāddha, requiring fresh commencement after purity is restored.

citations.quote: what is said by Hemādri, that in the abhyāsa option, the giving of the fee is at the end and the Brahmin is one, that is to be reconsidered
citations.justification: The Vīramitrodaya cites Hemādri's position and then subjects it to critique, using the digest as a major reference point.

citations.quote: The secondary time (gauṇakāla) for not performing the śrāddha in Mahālaya is stated in the Hemādri
citations.justification: The Vīramitrodaya quotes Hemādri as the source-text that preserves a Yama verse on secondary timing.

citations.quote: In the Nāgarakhaṇḍa: Even when the fortnight of the ancestors has passed, as long as the sun is in Virgo, / the ancestors desire the śrāddha given by their sons.
citations.justification: The Nāgarakhaṇḍa (a Purāṇic khaṇḍa) is cited for its description of ancestors waiting for śrāddha during the Virgo-Libra solar months.

citations.quote: This is from the Bhaviṣya.
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited for the verse on Dīpānvitā (new moon of Kārtika) as a secondary śrāddha occasion.

citations.quote: This is from the Matsya Purāṇa.
citations.justification: The Matsya Purāṇa is cited for the verse equating Bharaṇī śrāddha with the Gayā śrāddha.

citations.quote: Likewise, (Manu Smṛti, a. 3, ślo. 273) Whatever is mixed with honey, one should give on Trayodaśī.
citations.justification: Manu Smṛti 3.273 is cited with specific reference as authority for the Trayodaśī śrāddha prescription.

citations.quote: Likewise, (Manu Smṛti, a. 3, ślo. 274) May he be in our family who would give us on Trayodaśī / rice pudding with honey and ghee, in the eastern shadow of an elephant.
citations.justification: Manu Smṛti 3.274 is cited with specific reference, used in the hermeneutical discussion as an arthavāda verse.

citations.quote: Manu says: (a. 3, ślo. 277) By performing it on even nakṣatras, he obtains all desires.
citations.justification: Manu Smṛti 3.277 is cited for the rule on even versus odd nakṣatras in optional śrāddha.

citations.quote: Likewise, in the Yogiyājñavalkya: In the rainy season, on Trayodaśī, and in Maghā especially.
citations.justification: The Yogiyājñavalkya is explicitly named and quoted for its ruling on Trayodaśī śrāddha.

citations.quote: Yājñavalkya says: (a. 1, śrā. pra. 265-268) Heaven, offspring, vigor, valor, land, and strength…from Kṛttikā to Bharaṇī, he obtains these desires
citations.justification: Yājñavalkyasmṛti 1.265-268 is cited with specific verse references for the optional śrāddha fruits by nakṣatra.

citations.quote: This is from the Brahma Purāṇa.
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the verse on extended Mahālaya śrāddha timing through the Libra transit.

citations.quote: Because in this verse from the Candrikā, having stated the plain tithi, praise is stated for the conjunction with Maghā.
citations.justification: The Candrikā (a nibandha text) is cited for the verse distinguishing the plain Trayodaśī from the Trayodaśī-Maghā conjunction and their respective merits.

citations.quote: This is from the Viṣṇudharmottara.
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is cited for the verse declaring specific śrāddha tithis (including Trayodaśī) obligatory under pain of hell.

citations.quote: Another special rule should be seen in the Śrāddhaprakāśa.
citations.justification: The Śrāddhaprakāśa is referred to for additional detail on Trayodaśī, showing it as a parallel digest consulted for supplementary rules.

citations.quote: Another detailed discussion on this should be known in the Śrāddhaprakāśa.
citations.justification: The Śrāddhaprakāśa is again cross-referenced for detailed discussion of the Caturdaśī śrāddha.

citations.quote: In the Nāgarakhaṇḍa: For those who have an untimely death, or a death by a weapon…a śrāddha should be performed for them on Caturdaśī
citations.justification: The Nāgarakhaṇḍa is cited a second time, here for the expanded list of death-types warranting Caturdaśī śrāddha.

citations.quote: In the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa: He whose ancestors are young, or have died, or have been killed by a weapon, / by him it should be performed on Caturdaśī.
citations.justification: The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is cited for a verse on Caturdaśī śrāddha for those with young or violently deceased ancestors.

citations.quote: Youth is from the sixteenth year to the thirtieth year, say the Śrāddhaviveka and others.
citations.justification: The Śrāddhaviveka is cited for the legal definition of 'youth' relevant to the Caturdaśī śrāddha qualification.

citations.quote: In the Saṅgraha: A daughter's son, even if just born, and even if the maternal uncle is present, / should perform the śrāddha for the maternal grandfather on the bright Pratipad of Āśvina.
citations.justification: The Saṅgraha (a digest) is cited for the rule that the daughter's son has priority in performing the maternal grandfather's śrāddha on Āśvina Pratipad.

citations.quote: This should be taken when it pervades the forenoon (saṅgava), says the Nirṇayadīpa
citations.justification: The Nirṇayadīpa is cited for the rule on which portion of the day (forenoon) the Pratipad must cover for the daughter's son's śrāddha to be valid.

citations.quote: In the Viṣṇudharmottara: The ingress of the sun is praised for a śrāddha, O lord of the earth!
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is cited again for the general rule praising solar ingress and solstices as śrāddha occasions.

citations.quote: This is from the Viṣṇu Purāṇa.
citations.justification: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa is cited for the verse making śrāddha at lunar and solar eclipses obligatory.

citations.quote: The Nigama: In the dark fortnight, on whichever day one has the means, or on the new moon day, but especially on the Aṣṭakā…one should wish to perform it.
citations.justification: The Nigama (a scriptural/smṛti text) is cited for the broad permissibility of śrāddha whenever materials and a Brahmin are available.

citations.quote: In the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa: On obtaining a distinguished Brahmin, at an eclipse of the sun and moon, at a solstice…one should perform a śrāddha if one wishes.
citations.justification: The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is cited again for the comprehensive list of special optional śrāddha occasions.

citations.quote: In the Brahma Purāṇa: The śrāddha that is to be performed on the full moon days, in the ṛkṣa of the object, / at the conjunction of the month and the nakṣatra.
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the rule on full-moon-day śrāddha at the conjunction of month and nakṣatra.

citations.quote: A special rule for the full moon day of Bhādrapada is in the Brahma Purāṇa: For the Nāndīmukha ancestors…as is the word of Varāha.
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the Nāndīmukha ancestor category and their special full-moon śrāddha in Virgo.

citations.quote: In the Matsya Purāṇa: On Vaiśākhī, at an eclipse, and likewise, O child, in Mahālaya.
citations.justification: The Matsya Purāṇa is cited for the special mention of Vaiśākhī full moon as a śrāddha occasion.

citations.quote: In the Viṣṇudharmottara: In the dark fortnight of Āśvina, and in the first of Kārtika, / he who always performs a śrāddha obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha.
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is cited for the exceptional merit of Āśvina dark-fortnight śrāddha equated with the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

citations.quote: In the Viṣṇu Purāṇa: The third of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha…these four tithis are said by the ancients to be Yugādyās, of infinite merit.
citations.justification: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa is the primary authority cited for the canonical list of four Yugādi tithis.

citations.quote: In the Nāgarakhaṇḍa: Now listen, O lord of kings, to the Yugādyās, dear to the ancestors
citations.justification: The Nāgarakhaṇḍa is cited a third time, here for its Yugādi list and their cosmic-scale merit.

citations.quote: In the Matsya Purāṇa: The Tṛtīyā of Vaiśākha, and the Navamī of Kārttika…these are remembered as Yugādis
citations.justification: The Matsya Purāṇa is cited for its version of the Yugādi list.

citations.quote: In the Brahma Purāṇa, beginning with 'On the Tṛtīyā of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha was the Kṛta age'— These four tithis are Yugādyās
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the Yugādi list with cosmological grounding in the beginning of the Kṛta age.

citations.quote: In the Bhaviṣya: The Tṛtīyā of Vaiśākha is equal to the Kṛta age. / The Navamī in Kārttika is equal to the Tretā age.
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited for its version of the Yugādi tithis correlated with specific cosmic ages.

citations.quote: In the Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa: When the moon and the sun, and when Tiṣya and Bṛhaspati, / shall come together in one sign, then Kṛta will enter.
citations.justification: The Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa is cited for an astronomical prophecy about the return of the Kṛta age used in the Yugādi discussion.

citations.quote: from the Brahmavaivarta, 'and on the Paurṇamāsī of Māgha, the terrible Kaliyuga'
citations.justification: The Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa is cited in the discussion of which lunar day of Māgha corresponds to which cosmic age.

citations.quote: In the Nāradīya and Bhaviṣyottara: Two in the bright, and two in the dark, the poets know as Yugādyās.
citations.justification: The Nāradīya and Bhaviṣyottara are jointly cited for the rule dividing Yugādis between bright and dark fortnight and specifying morning versus afternoon timing.

citations.quote: In the Āditya Purāṇa: Where the day-nakṣatra is Revatī, and the passage into the signs, / that is the day of the end of an age; a gift there is infinite.
citations.justification: The Āditya Purāṇa is cited as the authority for the definition and merit of Yugānta (end-of-age) days.

citations.quote: A special rule is in the Brahma Purāṇa: At the sun's ingress into Leo, is the end of the Kṛta age.
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the specific solar-ingress definitions of Yugānta by zodiac sign.

citations.quote: In the Padma Purāṇa: On the Yugādis and at the Yugāntas, bathing, giving, recitation, etc., / whatever is done, its fruit is said to be that of the end of an age.
citations.justification: The Padma Purāṇa is cited for the general statement equating Yugādi and Yugānta merit with cosmic-age fruit.

citations.quote: In the Mātsya: The bright Navamī of Āśvayuj, and Dvādaśī of Kārttika…these are the Manvantarādis, making what is given imperishable.
citations.justification: The Mātsya Purāṇa is the primary authority for the extended list of fourteen Manvantarādi tithis.

citations.quote: In the Nāgarakhaṇḍa: Now, O king, the auspicious tithis called Kalpādis are stated…these thirty are the Kalpas, the tithis of the Supreme Lord.
citations.justification: The Nāgarakhaṇḍa is cited as the primary source for the list of thirty Kalpa-commencement tithis.

citations.quote: In the Matsya Purāṇa, however, other tithis are stated as Kalpādis.
citations.justification: The Matsya Purāṇa is cited for an alternative (shorter) list of Kalpādi tithis differing from the Nāgarakhaṇḍa list.

citations.quote: In the Vārāha Purāṇa: A gift on the new moon day is a hundred times the merit; on a day-elision, a hundred times that…At a Vyatīpāta, the gift is immeasurable
citations.justification: The Vārāha Purāṇa is the primary authority cited for the graduated hundred-fold merit scale culminating in Vyatīpāta.

citations.quote: The fruit of this is in the Narasiṃha Purāṇa: The fruit is a hundred thousand times at its arising; in its revolution, it is said to be a crore.
citations.justification: The Narasiṃha Purāṇa is cited for the specific graduated merit of the four phases of Vyatīpāta yoga.

citations.quote: The Kalpataru says that Vyatīpāta is the equality of the declination of the sun and moon, which is to be known from the science of astronomy.
citations.justification: The Kalpataru (a major nibandha digest) is cited for the astronomical definition of Vyatīpāta as solar-lunar declination equality.

citations.quote: In the Liṅga Purāṇa: Even with all one's wealth, a śrāddha should be performed at the sight of Rāhu.
citations.justification: The Liṅga Purāṇa is cited for the obligatory nature of the eclipse śrāddha, underscored by 'even with all one's wealth.'

citations.quote: In the Viṣṇudharmottara: At the ripening of the vrīhi rice, it should be performed, and likewise at the ripening of the barley.
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is cited for the obligatory new-grain śrāddha at the ripening of rice and barley crops.

citations.quote: In the Brahma Purāṇa: In the bright fortnight, having known the new grain to be ripe and beautiful, / one should go according to the rules of the field
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for prescribing bright-fortnight timing and ritual procedure for the new-grain śrāddha.

citations.quote: The prohibition of the dark fortnight is in the Kāmadhenu: A man should not perform the new grain rite in the dark fortnight
citations.justification: The Kāmadhenu is cited for the prohibition of dark-fortnight new-grain śrāddha.

citations.quote: In the Jyotiṣa: On a Nandā tithi, on a Friday, on Trayodaśī, in the three birth-nakṣatras, / one should not perform the new grain śrāddha
citations.justification: The Jyotiṣa science is cited for specific tithi and nakṣatra prohibitions applying to the new-grain śrāddha.

citations.quote: There, in the Brahma Purāṇa: Year after year, it should be performed for one's mother and father on the day of death.
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited as the authority for the annual death-anniversary (kṣayāha) śrāddha obligation.
